stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of porphyrias?
rationale: The porphyrias are a group of diseases caused by abnormalities in the pathway of porphyrin biosynthesis.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which substance is transported by hemoproteins?
rationale: Heme proteins are ubiquitous in biology and serve diverse functions including, but not limited to, oxygen transport and storage (eg, hemoglobin and myoglobin) and electron transport (eg, cytochrome c and cytochrome P450).
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > PORPHYRINS

stem: ALAS2 is converted into which substance?
rationale: Humans express two isozymes of ALA synthase: ALAS1 and ALAS2. ALAS1 is ubiquitously expressed throughout the body.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HEME IS SYNTHESIZED FROM SUCCINYL-CoA & GLYCINE

stem: ALA dehydratase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Following the formation of δ-aminolevulinate, it exits into the cytosol where ALA dehydratase catalyzes the condensation of two molecules of ALA to form porphobilinogen (Figure 31–4).
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HEME IS SYNTHESIZED FROM SUCCINYL-CoA & GLYCINE

stem: ALA dehydratase requires which substance for optimal activity?
rationale: ALA dehydratase requires an Fe-S cofactor for optimal activity.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HEME IS SYNTHESIZED FROM SUCCINYL-CoA & GLYCINE

stem: Hydroxymethylbilane is converted into which substance?
rationale: Hydroxymethylbilane is formed from the condensation of four molecules of porphobilinogen.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HEME IS SYNTHESIZED FROM SUCCINYL-CoA & GLYCINE

stem: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase catalyzes the decarboxylation of all four acetate moieties of uroporphyrinogen III to form coproporphyrinogen III (Figure 31–6).
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HEME IS SYNTHESIZED FROM SUCCINYL-CoA & GLYCINE

stem: Ferrochelatase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Ferrochelatase (heme synthase) catalyzes the incorporation of ferrous iron into protoporphyrin III. The incorporation of ferrous iron into protoporphyrin III is illustrated in Figure 31-7.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HEME IS SYNTHESIZED FROM SUCCINYL-CoA & GLYCINE

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of X-linked sideroblastic anemia?
rationale: Mutations in the gene encoding ALA synthase cause X-linked sideroblastic anemia. X-linked sideroblastic anemia is not a porphyria.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HEME IS SYNTHESIZED FROM SUCCINYL-CoA & GLYCINE

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of poisoning?
rationale: Lead poisoning causes elevated urinary levels of coproporphyrin.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > DISORDERS OF HEME BIOSYNTHESIS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of photosensitivity?
rationale: The oxidation of these porphyrinogens results in photosensitivity to visible light of about 400-nm wavelength.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > DISORDERS OF HEME BIOSYNTHESIS > Subsequent Metabolic Blocks

stem: Which substance is synthesised by ALAS1?
rationale: Derepression of synthesis of ALAS1 results in increased levels of potentially harmful heme precursors.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CLASSIFICATION OF THE PORPHYRIAS > Drug-Induced Porphyria

stem: Globin is converted into which substance?
rationale: The globin is degraded to its constituent amino acids. The released iron enters the iron pool.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN

stem: Reticuloendothelial cells are found within which structure?
rationale: The iron-free porphyrin portion of heme is also degraded, mainly in the reticuloendothelial cells of the liver, spleen, and bone marrow.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN

stem: Hemoglobin is converted into which substance?
rationale: Bilirubin is derived principally from hemoglobin. Bilirubin is derived with contributions from ineffective erythropoiesis and the catabolism of other heme proteins.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN

stem: Which substance is transported by serum albumin?
rationale: Bilirubin is bound by serum albumin for transport to the liver.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Bilirubin Is Transported to the Liver Bound to Serum Albumin

stem: Bilirubin is converted into which substance?
rationale: Most of the bilirubin excreted in the bile of mammals is bilirubin diglucuronide.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Secretion of Bilirubin Into the Bile

stem: Which substance is transported by hepatocytes?
rationale: Bilirubin dissociates from albumin and is taken up at the sinusoidal surface of hepatocytes by a large capacity facilitated transport system.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Uptake of Bilirubin by Liver Parenchymal Cells

stem: Which substance is transported by conjugated bilirubin?
rationale: Conjugated bilirubin is secreted into the bile by an active transport mechanism.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Secretion of Bilirubin Into the Bile

stem: Plasma membrane is found within which structure?
rationale: The protein involved in this transport is a multispecific organic anion transporter (MOAT), located in the plasma membrane of the bile canaliculi.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Secretion of Bilirubin Into the Bile

stem: Which condition is a recognized cause of obstructive jaundice?
rationale: When bilirubin conjugates exist abnormally in human plasma, such as in obstructive jaundice, they are predominantly monoglucuronides.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Secretion of Bilirubin Into the Bile

stem: In which structure are urobilinogens primarily found?
rationale: Most of the colorless urobilinogens formed in the colon are oxidized to colored urobilins.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Intestinal Bacteria Reduce Conjugated Bilirubin to Urobilinogen

stem: Urobilinogens are converted into which substance?
rationale: The feces are darkened by the oxidation of residual urobilinogens to urobilins upon standing in air.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > CATABOLISM OF HEME PRODUCES BILIRUBIN > Intestinal Bacteria Reduce Conjugated Bilirubin to Urobilinogen

stem: Which condition is a recognized cause of hyperbilirubinemia?
rationale: Crigler-Najjar syndrome types I and II are causes of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Occurrence of Unconjugated Bilirubin in Blood

stem: Which condition is a recognized cause of encephalopathy?
rationale: Hyperbilirubinemic toxic encephalopathy, or kernicterus, can result in mental retardation if left untreated.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Neonatal “Physiologic Jaundice”

stem: Which condition is a recognized cause of obstruction of the biliary tree?
rationale: Cancer of the head of the pancreas is a common cause of obstruction of the biliary tree.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Occurrence of Unconjugated Bilirubin in Blood

stem: Phototherapy is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phototherapy converts a portion of unconjugated bilirubin to derivatives that are excreted in the bile.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Neonatal “Physiologic Jaundice”

stem: Which condition is a recognized cause of congenital jaundice?
rationale: Type I Crigler-Najjar syndrome causes severe congenital jaundice with bilirubin levels exceeding 20 mg/dL in serum.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Type I Crigler-Najjar Syndrome

stem: Which condition is a recognized cause of brain damage?
options: obstruction of the common bile duct
rationale: The brain damage associated with type I Crigler-Najjar syndrome is a consequence of the severe jaundice.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Type I Crigler-Najjar Syndrome

stem: Which condition is a recognized cause of elevated plasma bilirubin levels?
rationale: Phototherapy is used to reduce plasma bilirubin levels in type I Crigler-Najjar syndrome.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Type I Crigler-Najjar Syndrome

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of liver dysfunction?
rationale: Chloroform can cause toxin-induced liver dysfunction.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Toxic Hyperbilirubinemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of conjugated hyperbilirubinemia?
rationale: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia commonly results from blockage of the hepatic or common bile ducts.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Obstruction in the Biliary Tree Is the Most Common Cause of Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of micro obstruction of?
rationale: Micro obstruction of intrahepatic biliary ductules can occur in infectious hepatitis.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Obstruction in the Biliary Tree Is the Most Common Cause of Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of micro obstruction of intrahepatic biliary ductules?
rationale: Micro obstruction of intrahepatic biliary ductules can occur in infectious hepatitis.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Obstruction in the Biliary Tree Is the Most Common Cause of Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hemolytic jaundice?
rationale: The combination of increased urobilinogen and absence of bilirubin is suggestive of hemolytic jaundice. Increased blood destruction from any cause brings about an increase in urine urobilinogen.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Urinary Urobilinogen & Bilirubin Are Clinical Indicators

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hepatitis?
options: obstruction of the common bile duct
answer: obstruction of the common bile duct
rationale: Hepatitis and obstruction of the common bile duct cause choluric jaundice. The jaundice of hemolytic anemia is referred to as acholuric.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments > HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA CAUSES JAUNDICE > Urinary Urobilinogen & Bilirubin Are Clinical Indicators

stem: Succinyl-CoA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Synthesis of heme commences with the condensation of succinyl-CoA and glycine to form ALA. This reaction is catalyzed by ALAS1, the regulatory enzyme of heme biosynthesis.
citation: chapter_31_porphyrins_and_bile_pigments — Porphyrins & Bile Pigments
